explanation: Bisect candidate values using the count C(m) of all entries at most midpoint m, comparing that count with the m available values in 1..m. Keep the half whose endpoint counts still bracket excess population.
correctness: Maintain C(lower-1)<=lower-1 and C(upper)>upper. Initially C(0)=0 and C(n)=n+1. If C(mid)>mid, set upper=mid; otherwise set lower=mid+1. At the final value v, C(v)>v and C(v-1)<=v-1, so their difference, the number of v entries, is at least two. This argument does not assume that C(m)>m is monotone.
walkthrough: For [1,3,4,2,3], lower=1 and upper=4. At midpoint 2, C(2)=2, so lower becomes 3. At midpoint 3, C(3)=4>3, so upper becomes 3. Return 3. Counts cover the whole prefix 1..midpoint, not just the current interval; the endpoint invariant guarantees that the final value repeats.
edgeCases: [1,1] returns 1 without a counting pass. Multiple repeated values are allowed; any actual duplicate passes.
timeComplexity: O(n log n) time: halving the n-value search interval takes O(log n) rounds, each scanning all n+1 entries.
spaceComplexity: O(1) auxiliary space: interval endpoints, midpoint and count only; input is read-only.
